pageProps.title: Ordeal by Innocence
pageProps.review: A review of Agatha Christie's novel Ordeal by Innocence, which deals with the uncomfortable truth brought about by the acquittal of a family member and the narrative structure of the original work that is differentiated from the drama.
pageProps.description: Truth was not the victory of justice, but the pain that destroyed everything
pageProps.content:
## Review The innocence of a family member has been proven, but rather than rejoicing, it's unpleasant and uncomfortable that chaos has returned to the once-peaceful household. It's an uncomfortable truth. Jacko was falsely accused, but he probably wasn't purely innocent in character.
Neither ```Poirot``` nor ```Miss Marple``` appears. This book has a narrative structure closer to a family drama than a traditional mystery novel.
It was also produced as a BBC drama, but the ending is different and the characters' psychology is different. It feels like they only took the general flow.
